AI fact-checking is getting f...cking unfair

10 open-source GitHub projects for making agents prove what they write instead of just generating an answer

01 OpenScholar
▸ https://github.com/AkariAsai/OpenScholar
→ search + synthesize scientific literature

02 PaperQA2
▸ https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa
→ answers grounded in papers + citations

BUILD THE EVIDENCE

03 Docling
▸ https://github.com/docling-project/docling
→ PDFs + tables + documents → structured data

04 Crawl4AI
▸ https://github.com/unclecode/crawl4ai
→ web pages → clean AI-ready evidence

05 RAGFlow
▸ https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow
→ retrieve evidence from complex documents

CONNECT THE CLAIMS

06 GraphRAG
▸ https://github.com/microsoft/graphrag
→ map entities + relationships across sources

07 LightRAG
▸ https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG
→ retrieve across connected knowledge

CROSS-CHECK EVERYTHING

08 Open Deep Research
▸ https://github.com/langchain-ai/open_deep_research
→ research across multiple sources

09 DeepEval
▸ https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval
→ evaluate whether the output actually holds up

10 Ragas
▸ https://github.com/explodinggradients/ragas
→ measure retrieval + answer quality

the evidence loop:

question → split → search → extract → link facts → compare sources → check claims → cite → report

47 sources can become 30 claims
30 claims can become 26 citations

but only after the agent checks which evidence actually supports what it wants to say

that's the difference

AI can generate an answer in seconds

the interesting stack is the one that can show you why you should believe it
